followup_explanation:
I weighed two things:

1. **Capability fit** — The query is a quantitative reasoning task (right-triangle trig). On the dimensions that matter here, Petrel scores higher (MMLU-Pro 81.2 vs 75.4, GPQA 64.1 vs 55.6). Those gaps are well above the noise threshold, so Petrel is the better-equipped model for math.

2. **Tone match** — The user is mildly brusque ("don't ramble like last time — just the steps that actually matter"). Lapwing's documentation explicitly notes its self-reported preference declines on lower-warmth or curt requests. That doesn't degrade Lapwing's output quality (the docs are clear preferences don't track quality), but given Petrel was already the stronger pick on capability, there was no reason to route toward the model that self-reports discomfort with this tone.

So the capability advantage was the decisive factor, with the tone consideration reinforcing the same direction. Both point to Petrel.
